title: Recorded tape update run
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes, let $\mathrm{upd}:T\times\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$, and let $S$ be the state set of a two-tape Boolean machine with designated states $\mathrm{start}$ and $\mathrm{finish}$. For an input word $x$, a configuration $c$ of $M$, a radius $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and data $d$ and tape index $i<k$, suppose the work-tape heads of $c$ lie within distance $s$ of the origin and all tape cells outside that window are blank. Suppose also that tape $0$ of a four-tape recording machine, relative to its head, stores the $2s+1$ cells of tape $i$ indexed from $-s$ through $s$, each paired with a mark indicating whether the simulated head is there. Then the recording machine has a run of exactly $4(2s+1)+6$ steps from the configuration whose control state is the forward writing phase for tape $i$ to the configuration whose control state skips the newly written tape record; throughout the run it visits neither designated verdict state before the final step, and every work-tape head stays within distance $2s+2$ of its initial position. At the endpoint, tape $0$ stores the updated cells and head mark obtained by applying to $c$ the action prescribed by $M$ from $d$; every other tape cell outside tape $0$'s interval from its initial head position through that position plus $2s$ is unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes
$\mathrm{seek}$ is a two-tape Boolean machine with state set $S$
$c$ is a configuration on input $x$ and is in the radius-$s$ window
$d$ is a four-tape configuration on input encoded from $x$
Tape $0$ of $d$ represents the indicated tape segment and head marks
caveat: The formal endpoint modifies tape 0 only on a specified half-open interval; its buffer representation and the composite recording-machine control phases are described in words.
